decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with a rising elbow-up arc; orient gripper downward gradually, right arm parked.
Advance above the left tube while finishing most of the downward wrist rotation; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Lower toward the left tube center with open jaws, using RGB-derived tube axis for alignment.
Visually refine grasp along the tube toward its cap before closing; wrist view currently favors the tip.
Close around the centered tube body, then lift slightly to verify visual retention.
Tube appears retained. Lift clear and begin rotating it upright while moving toward the rack's left slots.
Carry retained tube toward the rack while smoothly rotating upright; keep clear of the rack top.
Finish upright orientation above a left-side large rack hole; hold closed and assess alignment before insertion.
Approach the left rack opening vertically with a small forward alignment correction; retain the tube for visual depth checking.
Slowly lower the upright tube into the apparent left-front large opening; make a small rearward centering correction.
Release the supported tube and retreat with open jaws to inspect whether it remains upright in the rack.
First tube remains upright in its slot. Retract left arm toward home and start an elbow-up approach to the outer right tube.
Continue right-arm approach above the outer tube, aligning to its slanted axis; left arm retracts without crossing.
Center and descend around the outer right tube using wrist-view lateral and axis corrections; finish left-arm return.
Refine right-tube grasp nearer the cap and correct the visible axis tilt before closing.
Shift the grasp slightly down the tube body, close, and start a small retention-check lift.
Lift the retained right tube well clear of the table and begin its upright rotation toward the rack.
Transfer the retained tube inward in the right workspace while continuing a smooth upright rotation.
Finish upright positioning over a right-side large opening; pause above the rack to inspect alignment.
Center the upright right tube over the rack's right-front opening while lowering cautiously toward insertion height.
Lower the upright right tube straight into the aligned opening, keeping the grasp closed until depth is checked.
Tube appears to have contacted a rim and shifted in the grasp. Lift clear and recenter toward the rightmost large opening before retrying.
Retry a slow vertical descent at the corrected large-hole alignment; monitor tube motion relative to the jaws.
Continue a shallow, slow insertion; the tube is now centered over the large opening but shifted higher in the grasp.
Tube is still catching the rim. Lift and shift a few millimeters toward the visible large-hole center rather than pushing farther.
The large opening is now visibly centered below the tube tip. Lower gently to engage it, then pause to inspect.
Correct the remaining fore-aft rim offset with a short lift and inward shift; avoid further forced descent.
Gently engage the centered opening and open the jaws so the tube can settle under gravity; inspect before retreating.
Withdraw the open gripper from the rack surface to let the tube settle freely and inspect its support.
Clear the rack with open jaws to inspect the second tube, which appears tilted rather than securely seated.
Approach the tilted second tube's upper body with open jaws to recover it and straighten before reseating.
Regrasp the second tube's upper body gently, with the rack supporting its tip; inspect before lifting.
Lift the regrasped tilted tube clear of the rack before correcting its angle; keep the jaws closed.
Rotate the recovered tube away from its lean toward the gripper, with clearance above the rack; assess its axis before reseating.
Continue correcting the tube's strong lean while raising the wrist to keep its tip clear; compensate the gripper offset during rotation.
Previous command was not executed. Retry the tilt correction at half increments to maintain joint continuity.
The head view now shows the tube near vertical; make a smaller corrective rotation and bring its tip toward the right opening.
Continue controlled tube-axis correction with added clearance; the cap obscures the wrist view, so approach remains conservative.
Correct the remaining lateral lean seen in the head view and translate the tube tip toward the right-front opening.
The recovered tube now appears upright. Engage the right-front opening slowly with a small centering adjustment.
Complete a short seating descent and release the now-upright recovered tube to settle into the opening.
The second tube settled beside the opening. Regrasp it at its lower settled height for a small rack-relative correction.
The second tube fell onto the table. Open and lift clear, then reorient for a fresh body grasp along its new axis.
Continue the clear, open-jaw reorientation above the fallen tube, matching its new table axis.
Continue gradual wrist alignment over the fallen tube while staying above contact height.
Finish top-down alignment with the fallen tube and descend toward a fresh near-cap body grasp.
Lower around the fallen tube body and refine the visible tube-axis alignment; keep open until centering is confirmed.
The open jaws contacted nearby geometry. Narrow the approach near the cap, close on the body, and make a small test lift.
The previous closure missed. Reopen and center over the separated tube on the wrist image's left, then descend with corrected axis.
Narrow the open jaws to avoid the adjacent tube and refine centering over the target body with a shallow descent.
Close on the now-centered tube body after a short descent, then test retention with a small lift.
